narrative: Material PL1__MB5A55F8 exhibits a smooth, normally distributed daily demand (CV=0.17) with a statistically significant downward trend over the observation window. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.55), necessitating a robust safety stock of 154,164 units at the 95% service level. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 1,433,992 units yields a 69.1% reduction in total annual inventory costs versus the current SAP parameterisation, while respecting the storage capacity constraint (72.3% utilisation).

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and normally distributed (CV=0.17, 100% non-zero), making the classic (r,Q) framework analytically valid and computationally straightforward. The high-volume, low-unit-cost profile means ordering cost dominates, and the EOQ of ~1.43M units correctly prescribes infrequent large batches over the SAP MOQ-sized replenishments.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Capacity utilisation at 72.3% leaves adequate headroom. No capacity constraint binds. If demand recovers to peak levels (~140K/day), the reorder point should be reviewed upward.
